Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old male with history of asthma presents with 3-hour history of chest tightness, shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough following recent cold; ran out of asthma inhalers.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Chest tightness for 3 hours.
- Associated symptoms: Mild shortness of breath, wheeze, cough (non-productive), cough persists after cold, worse on exertion (e.g., stairs), not at rest; recent sore throat, runny nose (improved).
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no shortness of breath at rest, no cough productive of sputum.
- Past medical history: Asthma (previous severe exacerbation—hospital admission and intubation at age 16-17), hay fever, allergy to dust, childhood eczema, childhood milk protein allergy.
- Allergies: No drug allergies.
- Medications: Previously prescribed Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler and Clenil Modulite (steroid) inhaler; has not used either for past week due to running out.
- Social history/preventive care: Not detailed.

Examination:

- No physical exam or vitals documented.

Impression:
- Asthma exacerbation likely triggered by recent viral illness and missed asthma medication.

Plan:
- Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Prescribe Clenil Modulite inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Prescribe 5-day course of oral steroids (specific medication, dose/route/frequency not documented; instructions: 2 tablets in the morning).
- Prescribe a spacer device.
- Advise use of Ventolin as needed (PRN); seek medical attention if needing Ventolin more than every 3 hours.
- Rest recommended; time off work advised.
- Safety netting: Seek urgent medical attention if symptoms worsen (increased shortness of breath, chest tightness, light-headedness, or other concerning symptoms).

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies documented but medications reconciliation incomplete (full medication list/doses/routes/frequencies not documented).
  - No examination or vital signs performed.
  - No details on smoking status or social history.
  - No documentation of peak flow or objective assessment of severity.
  - No specific oral steroid prescribed by name.

● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.

● Transcript quality:
  - Good quality; clear history. Some technical interruptions, but adequate clinical information for assessment.
